A few useful design principles for **Heliana-style shops**:

1. **Every shop should care about different monster parts.**  
   A blacksmith wants bones, scales, shells, glands, and ores from monsters. An alchemist wants blood, venom, bile, spores, and organs. A cookhouse wants edible cuts, eggs, herbs, fats, and weird seasonings.

   Don’t make every recipe buyable. Let shops teach rare recipes after the party proves themselves, brings rare materials, saves the business, or completes a contract.

# Notes

Additional DM notes.

## Pricing Notes

- Use normal item prices when convenient.
- Adjust monster-part value by rarity, danger, freshness, legality, and shop specialization.
- Shops should not buy every part at full value.
- The more specialized the shop, the better prices it offers for its preferred materials.
- Rare recipes should often be rewards, not simple purchases.

## Tone Notes

This shop should make monster hunting feel like an economy, not just a loot table. Every jar, hide, fang, organ, recipe, and contract should imply a creature, a story, or a problem waiting to happen.

# Jimmyjock Labingi

**Jimmyjock Labingi** was a legendary bard, poet, and early leader of the [[Twothirdlings]] of [[content/Regions/private/Doobius House|Doobius House]]. He is best remembered as a sharp-tongued champion of his mother’s people and one of the loudest voices against Elyrian settlement of his maternal ancestral lands.

## Background

Jimmyjock was the illegitimate son of [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] and a native concubine whose real name has been almost entirely erased from official records. Surviving Elyrian documents refer to her only as **“Mary Halfling-woman,”** a label that says more about the recordkeepers than it does about her.

Though Jimmyjock was raised with an unusual level of education for the time, Duke Doobius never truly accepted him as a legitimate son, largely because Jimmyjock was not fully human. Doobius later married a human woman, fathered human heirs, and left his estate to them when he died, leaving Jimmyjock with neither inheritance nor recognition.

## Rise to Leadership

Rather than seek acceptance from the family that rejected him, Jimmyjock turned toward his mother’s people. A gifted bard, poet, and speaker, he became known as a man of the people: educated enough to argue with nobles, angry enough to mock them in verse, and beloved enough that common folk repeated his songs long after officials tried to silence them.

When Duke Doobius finally died, the [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, seized the moment. They claimed the estate and surrounding settlement as their own and elected Jimmyjock as their leader.

## Legacy

To the Twothirdlings, Jimmyjock Labingi is remembered as a folk hero: the disinherited son who chose his mother’s people over his father’s name. To Elyrian loyalists, he was a rebel, demagogue, and thief of noble property. Both versions agree on one thing: Jimmyjock knew exactly how to turn a song into a weapon.

## Traits

- **Role:** Legendary bard, poet, folk leader
- **Known For:** Anti-settler resistance, revolutionary songs, leadership of Doobius House
- **Personality:** Charismatic, defiant, witty, bitter toward noble hypocrisy
- **Ideal:** A people have the right to rule the land that remembers them.
- **Bond:** His erased mother and the Twothirdlings who claimed him as kin.
- **Flaw:** His hatred of Elyrian nobility could make compromise nearly impossible.

## Possible Sayings

> *“My father gave me no house, so my mother’s people gave me a homeland.”*

> *“A duke may own a deed. A people own the dirt beneath it.”*

> *“If they write your mother out of the records, sing her name louder.”*

# Molten Maw

**Molten Maw** is a colossal underground volcanic city in the [[Underdark]], inhabited mainly by [[Duergar]] and [[Svirfneblin]]. Built around a vast open caldera beneath the earth, the city serves as both a natural forge and a deadly hazard. Its streets are carved into black basalt terraces, iron gantries, cooled lava shelves, and tunnels reinforced against constant tremors.

Rivers of semi-intelligent, magically charged lava course through the city’s depths. Locals call these flows **the Red Veins**, and treat them less like ordinary magma and more like dangerous spirits of the earth. The lava sometimes changes course without warning, answers certain forms of elemental magic, or rises into half-formed elemental creatures that guard the flows from thieves, miners, and careless outsiders.

## Character

Molten Maw is brutal, smoky, rich, and paranoid. Every surface is warm. Every shadow glows faintly red. The air tastes of metal, ash, and old bargains. Duergar foundries hammer day and night, while Svirfneblin engineers maintain hidden vents, cooling chambers, pressure gates, and secret escape tunnels.

The city is famous for:

- Infernal heat and volcanic hazards
- Masterwork metal, obsidian, glass, and gemstone craft
- Hidden smuggler dens
- Elemental lava cults
- Political exiles and escaped criminals
- The underground black market known as [[The Silt Road]]

## The Silt Road

Criminals, rebels, fugitives, and desperate surface-folk sometimes flee to Molten Maw, surviving in fire-resistant cave networks and hidden market warrens. Over time, these routes became the heart of [[The Silt Road]], a literal underground criminal market that moves contraband, people, secrets, cursed goods, monster parts, and forbidden magic beneath the notice of surface authorities.

The Silt Road does not truly belong to any one faction. Duergar clans tax it, Svirfneblin guides navigate it, smugglers profit from it, and local gangs bleed for control of it.

## Notable Features

- **The Red Veins:** Semi-intelligent lava rivers that move through the city like living arteries.
- **The Chain Terraces:** Stacked residential districts connected by chains, lifts, bridges, and mine platforms.
- **The Cinder Warrens:** Smuggler caves, fugitive dens, and black-market stalls hidden behind cooling vents.
- **The Glass Forges:** Workshops where volcanic glass, enchanted slag, and fire-tempered gems are shaped.
- **The Ash Courts:** Harsh civic chambers where Duergar clan leaders, Svirfneblin engineers, and criminal brokers negotiate.
- **The Mouth Below:** A deeper volcanic pit believed to be either a planar wound, sleeping primordial, or the source of the Red Veins.

- Sudden lava surges
- Toxic gas pockets
- Collapsing tunnels
- Elemental guardians
- Duergar press gangs
- Svirfneblin sabotage traps

[new]
# Upper South Booftown

## The Ashtray

**Upper South Booftown**, better known as **The Ashtray**, is where the streets are rough, the air is thick with soot, and the law only exists if someone nearby is willing to enforce it. Wedged between the slow-churning lava flows of [[Mount Zooka]] and the more “civilized” parts of the city, The Ashtray is a district of smoke-blackened rooftops, crooked tenements, ash-slick alleys, and hustlers who can smell weakness through a closed door.

The native [[Halflings|halfling]] population makes up a significant portion of the district’s residents, though The Ashtray is also home to outcasts, fugitives, dock toughs, failed apprentices, smugglers, off-duty mercenaries, and anyone else too useful, desperate, or dangerous to fit anywhere cleaner. It is not a safe neighborhood, but it is an honest one in its own crooked way: everyone knows what everything costs, even if the price is not always paid in coin.

## Character

The Ashtray feels like a city stacked on top of itself. Buildings climb over one another in a tangled mess of shoddy construction, patched bridges, rooftop walkways, hanging laundry lines, and half-legal expansions. The ground level belongs to carts, gangs, gamblers, and stray dogs. The upper levels belong to lookouts, rooftop gardens, hidden grow rooms, and people who do not want to be found.

The air is always warm and dirty. Ash from [[Mount Zooka]] settles on windowsills, food stalls, shrine steps, and sleeping children. Locals joke that if you leave a white shirt outside overnight, it wakes up as part of the neighborhood.

## Power on the Streets

The [[Mandem on Booftown]] (MOB) and the [[Cough City Crew]] (CCC) fight an endless turf war over illicit [[Arcannabis]] strains, underground fight rings, protection rackets, backroom gambling, bootlegged [[Alcohol]], and black-market [[Magitech]]. Their conflict is loud enough to terrify outsiders but familiar enough that residents know when to duck, when to run, and when to pretend they saw nothing.

Neither gang fully controls The Ashtray. Power shifts block by block, rooftop by rooftop, and business by business. A tea shop might pay MOB on Mondays, CCC on Fridays, and a local auntie every day because everyone knows she is the one actually keeping the street alive.

## Notable Features

- **The Sootsteps:** A maze of exterior stairs, ladders, rope bridges, and rooftop shortcuts used by locals to avoid gang checkpoints.
- **Cinder Courts:** Open lots where dice games, fistfights, public arguments, and informal trials are held.
- **Backroom Taverns:** Hidden drinking halls serving bootlegged [[Alcohol]], bad decisions, and worse information.
- **Ash Gardens:** Rooftop planters where locals grow hardy food, medicinal herbs, and discreet [[Arcannabis]] strains under layers of volcanic grit.
- **The Black Stalls:** A shifting night market for stolen goods, rare poisons, counterfeit papers, and illegal [[Magitech]] parts.
- **Smoke Chapels:** Tiny street shrines where residents pray for protection, revenge, luck, or a clean death.

## Reputation

Despite its lawless reputation, Upper South Booftown is not just a den of crime. It is a proving ground. Fortunes are made and lost in a single dice roll. Gangsters rule like kings until someone hungrier takes their corner. Bounty hunters stalk their marks through smog-choked streets, and even the smallest [[Halflings]] can rise to power if they are clever, ruthless, and loved by the right people.

To outsiders, The Ashtray is dangerous. To locals, it is home.

## Adventure Hooks

- A gang truce collapses after someone steals a rare Arcannabis strain from a rooftop grow.
- A bounty target is hiding in the Sootsteps, protected by locals who hate the person hunting them.
- A batch of black-market Magitech starts malfunctioning and setting buildings on fire.
- A respected halfling elder asks the party to remove a gang lieutenant without starting a district war.
- A child finds something valuable, cursed, or alive in a fresh fall of ash from [[Mount Zooka]].
- The MOB and CCC both want the same monster part, and neither side knows why the other wants it.
>>>>>>> END

# N.E.R.D

**N.E.R.D**, short for **Nerds Enjoy Researching Data**, is an arcane educational institution in [[Stickyickistan]] dedicated to magical research, mathematical theory, glyphwork, history, planar studies, and experimental problem-solving.

The institution is known for producing brilliant scholars, eccentric mages, obsessive researchers, and the occasional overconfident disaster. Its halls are filled with lecture chambers, enchanted chalkboards, sealed archives, unstable student projects, and libraries containing books that probably should not be available to first-year students.

## Role in Stickyickistan

N.E.R.D serves as one of [[Stickyickistan|Stickyickistan’s]] major centers of arcane education and magical research. Its professors and students are often consulted by city officials, adventuring parties, merchants, and private patrons when a problem requires brains, spells, obscure citations, or dangerous fieldwork.

The institution maintains an uneasy relationship with practical power. It claims to pursue knowledge for its own sake, but its research is valuable to nobles, guilds, inventors, monster hunters, and political factions across the region.
